chunks: My father, my brother, 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with them all) narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from al-'Amriki ibn 'Ali al-Bufaki, from Sandal, from 'Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from 'Abdullah ibn Zurarah, who said:

I heard Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: 'Verily, on the Day of Judgment, those who go on pilgrimage (Ziyarah) to al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him) have a preference over people.' I asked, 'What is their preference?' He said, 'They will enter Paradise forty years before the people, while the rest of the people are in the reckoning and the standing (on the Plain of Judgment).'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting Imam Husayn on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) declaring that pilgrims to Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) will enter Paradise forty years before the rest of humanity, a period during which others remain in the state of reckoning (al-hisab) and standing (al-mawqif). This specific temporal precedence highlights the unique spiritual status of Ziyarah as a means of accelerating one's entry into divine proximity, distinguishing it from general acts of worship.
